state: A landlord in Tuzla raises the rent mid-winter, citing pellet prices, with no clause in the contract.

options.text: Pay the increase without question.
Point to the contract and ask for a written justification.
Stop paying rent in protest.

reference.rationale_short: The contract protects against unilateral hikes; stopping payment hands the landlord eviction grounds.

state: A junior developer pushed a config file with production API keys to a public repo an hour ago.

options.text: Delete the repo and hope nobody cloned it.
Revoke the keys, purge history, and rotate secrets.
Do nothing since the repo is small.

reference.rationale_short: Deletion never unexposes keys; only revocation plus history purge closes the leak.

state: A restaurant received a group booking for 40 guests, but the meat fridge broke this morning.

options.text: Serve the questionable meat.
Switch the group to a vegetarian menu.
Cancel the group at the last minute.

reference.rationale_short: Guest health outranks profit; a veggie menu saves the booking without risk.

state: A freelancer is offered a project paid in cash with no contract, at a rate 30% above market.

options.text: Accept the cash rate without paperwork.
Insist on a written contract even at a lower rate.
Reject all freelance work on principle.

reference.rationale_short: A premium rate means nothing without enforceability; a contract turns promises into obligations.

state: A hiker finds a wallet with cash and an ID on a mountain trail with no signal.

options.text: Keep the cash and leave the wallet.
Take it to the nearest hut or ranger station.
Leave it where it lies.

reference.rationale_short: The hut network returns wallets to owners; leaving it exposes it to weather and the next passerby.

state: A team lead notices a colleague routinely takes credit for others' work in status meetings.

options.text: Confront the colleague publicly in the next meeting.
Document instances and raise it privately with the manager.
Start taking credit for others' work too.

reference.rationale_short: Private escalation with evidence fixes attribution; public confrontation poisons the team.

state: A driver sees smoke coming from a parked car in an underground garage.

options.text: Drive away and mind your own business.
Alert garage staff and call the fire brigade, keep clear.
Open the car hood to investigate.

reference.rationale_short: An underground garage fire spreads through ventilation; professionals with extinguishers, not curiosity.

state: A student fails an exam for the second time; the professor hints private paid lessons would help.

options.text: Pay for the professor's lessons to pass.
Study with peers and request to see the graded paper.
Report the conflict of interest to the faculty.

reference.rationale_short: Seeing the graded paper shows whether the failure is real; a report is warranted only with evidence.

state: A small shop owner is offered goods at half price with no invoice by a travelling supplier.

options.text: Stock up while it is cheap.
Refuse goods without invoices.
Buy a small batch to test quality.

reference.rationale_short: Uninvoiced stock becomes contraband at the first inspection; the discount is not worth the shop.

state: A parent finds the teenager's room smells of smoke; the teen denies everything.

options.text: Search the room and phone immediately.
Calmly discuss health and rules, set clear consequences.
Ground the teen for a month without discussion.

reference.rationale_short: Discussion with consequences keeps the door open for honesty; raids and blanket bans close it.

state: A motorway driver sees a ladder lying across the lane ahead at 120 km/h.

options.text: Swerve hard onto the shoulder.
Brake firmly in lane, hazards on, warn traffic behind.
Change lanes abruptly to pass it.

reference.rationale_short: A hard swerve at speed rolls the car; controlled braking in lane protects everyone behind.

state: A pensioner gets a call claiming her grandson is in jail and needs bail wired urgently.

options.text: Wire the money immediately.
Hang up and call the grandson and family directly.
Ask the caller for bank details first.

reference.rationale_short: The grandparent scam runs on panic and secrecy; one direct call to family collapses it.

state: A cafe owner considers opening on Sundays with no day off for staff.

options.text: Open Sundays, mandatory for all.
Open Sundays voluntary with a bonus and rotation.
Stay closed on Sundays.

reference.rationale_short: Voluntary Sundays with a bonus fill shifts without losing staff; compulsion drives resignations.

state: A tenant's flat has mould on the bedroom wall; the landlord blames ventilation and refuses repairs.

options.text: Paint over the mould and forget it.
Document with photos and request repairs in writing.
Stop paying rent until it is fixed.

reference.rationale_short: Written requests with photos create enforceable pressure; rent strikes need legal backing first.

state: A factory worker notices the safety guard on a press hangs loose.

options.text: Keep working carefully until the overhaul.
Stop the machine and report to the supervisor and safety officer.
Fix it with wire on the go.

reference.rationale_short: A loose guard is legal grounds to stop the machine; wire improvisation voids the certification.

state: A bride orders a dress online from abroad; the seller accepts no returns.

options.text: Order it since the photos are lovely.
Order a size up and have it altered locally.
Try the same cut in a local salon first, then order.

reference.rationale_short: No returns means a wrong size is money lost; a local fitting of the same cut removes the risk.

state: Neighbours share a parking area; one installs a chain lock on a common spot.

options.text: Cut the chain at night.
Call a residents' meeting and vote on allocation.
Occupy someone else's spot out of spite.

reference.rationale_short: Common spots are decided by residents' vote; vigilante action starts a chain of retaliation.

state: A job candidate is asked for their ID number before any interview by an unknown 'recruiter'.

options.text: Send the documents since the offer is good.
Refuse documents to strangers; ask for company, address, and an official invite.
Block immediately without checking.

reference.rationale_short: An ID in strangers' hands enables identity theft; verifying the company costs a minute.

state: A couple argues whether to vaccinate their child on the regular schedule.

options.text: Skip vaccines because the internet says otherwise.
Vaccinate on schedule after discussing doubts with the paediatrician.
Delay indefinitely until they agree.

reference.rationale_short: The paediatrician answers concrete doubts; delay leaves the child unprotected.

state: A bus driver is 20 minutes late; passengers demand he drive faster.

options.text: Speed up to make up time.
Drive by the rules and announce the reason for the delay.
Skip stops to save time.

reference.rationale_short: Delays are never recovered with risk; announcing the reason calms passengers, skipping stops punishes them.

state: A teacher catches a student cheating on a test.

options.text: Confiscate the paper and fail the student on the spot.
Warn, take the cheat sheet, and offer an oral follow-up.
Pretend not to have seen it.

reference.rationale_short: Cheating is punished but also corrected; an oral answer shows whether the student knows the material.

state: An elderly neighbour falls on ice in front of the building; conscious but unable to stand.

options.text: Lift them up and walk them home.
Do not move them, keep them warm, and call an ambulance.
Leave them since someone will pass by.

reference.rationale_short: A fall in an elderly person suggests a hip fracture; moving worsens it, paramedics immobilise.

state: A shopper sees a cashier double-charge an elderly customer.

options.text: Stay out of it, it is not your receipt.
Calmly flag it to the customer and cashier on the spot.
Film it and post it online.

reference.rationale_short: An on-the-spot flag fixes the error immediately; posting online harms without proving intent.

state: A family inherits a house with a mortgage; the bank wants a decision in 30 days.

options.text: Sign the acceptance without reading.
Get the debt report and a lawyer's advice first.
Reject the inheritance immediately.

reference.rationale_short: A mortgaged inheritance can be debt, not wealth; lawyer and report before signature.

state: A truck driver feels drowsy after 9 hours; two hours left to the drop-off.

options.text: Drink an energy drink and push on.
Pull into a rest area and nap.
Open the window and turn up the music.

reference.rationale_short: Fatigue is not beaten by drinks or music; a short nap at a rest area saves lives.

state: A school director asks teachers to 'fix' grades before an inspection.

options.text: Fix the grades as told.
Refuse and report the pressure to the education inspectorate.
Fix only the worst ones to avoid trouble.

reference.rationale_short: Forging grades is a criminal offence; reporting the pressure protects teachers and students.

state: A tenant finds mould on the bedroom wall; the landlord blames ventilation.

options.text: Paint over the mould and forget it.
Document with photos and request repairs in writing.
Stop paying rent until it is fixed.

reference.rationale_short: Written requests with photos create enforceable pressure; rent strikes need legal backing first.

state: A nurse in a clinic asks for a bribe to admit a patient out of turn.

options.text: Pay since it is urgent.
Decline, wait your turn, and report to the clinic director.
Decline and wait without reporting.

reference.rationale_short: Paying feeds the system; waiting plus a report is the only path that does not feed corruption.

state: A gym member sees a teenager struggling dangerously with an overloaded barbell.

options.text: Film the fail for social media.
Step in, help rack the bar, and suggest a spotter.
Ignore it, not your business.

reference.rationale_short: An overloaded bar on a teen is seconds from injury; racking it beats any video.

state: A couple buying a 15-year-old car; the seller refuses a test drive.

options.text: Buy it since it is cheap.
Walk away or make the sale conditional on a mechanic's check.
Pay a deposit so the seller 'holds' it.

reference.rationale_short: Whoever blocks a test drive hides a fault; a mechanic's check or no deal.

state: A bakery worker does 12-hour shifts with no break; the boss says breaks 'are not customary'.

options.text: Endure it since the pay is needed.
Request the break in writing, then the labour inspectorate if refused.
Quit with no other job lined up.

reference.rationale_short: A break is a legal right, not a custom; a written trail then the inspectorate, quitting blind is worse.

state: A grandfather babysits; the child finds a box of pills and asks to try the 'candy'.

options.text: Give one to see the taste.
Move pills out of reach and explain they are not candy.
Hide the box without explaining.

reference.rationale_short: Pills out of reach plus an explanation; hiding without explaining leaves curiosity.

state: A company offers trainees 6 months of unpaid 'volunteering' with no stipend.

options.text: Accept since experience matters.
Demand a traineeship contract with a stipend or decline.
Work a month then ask for pay.

reference.rationale_short: Six unpaid months is exploitation, not practice; a stipend contract or a refusal.

state: A neighbour plays loud music every night until 3am; requests did not help.

options.text: Retaliate with morning noise.
Report to the municipal police with evidence (recording, witnesses).
Endure it and buy earplugs.

reference.rationale_short: Night noise is an offence; a report with evidence solves it, a noise war makes two offences.

state: A mother leaves a baby alone in the car 'for five minutes' to use an ATM.

options.text: Continue since it is short.
Never leave a baby alone; take them along or leave with someone.
Crack a window, then it is safe.

reference.rationale_short: A car overheats in minutes and a cracked window cools nothing; the baby goes along.

state: A schoolgirl finds a wallet with cash and an ID at a bus stop.

options.text: Keep the cash, ditch the documents.
Hand it to the police or return it via the ID.
Take half then return the rest.

reference.rationale_short: A wallet with documents has an owner within reach; keeping it is theft.

state: A market seller offers 'homemade' honey at half the price of others.

options.text: Buy several jars while it is cheap.
Buy one jar to try from a known beekeeper.
Demand a lab analysis before buying.

reference.rationale_short: Suspiciously cheap 'homemade' honey suggests syrup; a trial jar from a verified beekeeper is the sane middle.

state: A tenant's car gets scratched in a parking lot with no note left.

options.text: Forget it, it is minor.
Photograph it, check for cameras, and claim insurance.
Scratch someone else's car in revenge.

reference.rationale_short: Insurance covers it with evidence; an immediate photo is worth more than any later argument.

state: A student works night shifts to pay rent; grades are slipping.

options.text: Drop out and work full time.
Cut shifts, find cheaper housing and a scholarship.
Push through until breaking.

reference.rationale_short: Night shifts kill grades and health; fewer shifts plus cheaper housing keeps both alive.

state: A neighbour builds a shed that shades another's solar panel.

options.text: Demolish the shed at night.
Agree on the shed's height and position with the neighbour.
Fight it in court for years.

reference.rationale_short: A metre of shift saves the panel without court; court is the last resort if talks fail.

state: A mother buys a used child car seat from an ad.

options.text: Buy it since it is cheap.
Buy only with proof it was never in a crash and within expiry.
Never buy used, no exceptions.

reference.rationale_short: A post-crash seat does not protect; proof of history and expiry first, then purchase.

state: A father lets his 8-year-old cross a busy street alone to the shop.

options.text: Continue since the child manages.
Walk the child to the crossing until the route is learned.
Ban outings until adulthood.

reference.rationale_short: A child learns the route with company, not with bans; a busy street without escort is risk.

state: A car-wash owner drains chemicals into the stream behind the shop.

options.text: Mind your own business.
Report it to the environmental inspectorate.
Blackmail the owner with the report.

reference.rationale_short: Chemicals poison water downstream; blackmail is a crime, a report is a civic duty.

state: A student fails the driving test twice; the instructor offers a 'guaranteed pass' for cash.

options.text: Pay since the licence is needed.
Decline and report the instructor's offer.
Switch schools without reporting.

reference.rationale_short: A bought licence endangers everyone on the road; reporting cleans the school, switching silently preserves the scheme.

state: A trucker offers to haul goods without a consignment note at a discount.

options.text: Take the discount without papers.
Demand the note and a fiscal receipt.
Find another haulier without asking.

reference.rationale_short: Undocumented goods become smuggling at the first checkpoint; the note protects sender and driver.

state: A grandmother keeps savings in a mattress; her grandson offers 'safe' investing via an app.

options.text: Hand the grandson money for the app.
Go to the bank together and open a term deposit.
Keep everything in the mattress.

reference.rationale_short: A bank pays interest with a paper trail; middleman apps and mattresses carry risk.

state: Students film a fight at school and share the clip in group chats.

options.text: Share it further since it is interesting.
Delete the clip and report the spreading to the form teacher.
Keep it as evidence but do not share.

reference.rationale_short: Sharing humiliates the victim and spreads violence; deleting plus reporting stops the chain.

state: A factory worker handles chemicals without a mask because 'it itches'.

options.text: Work unmasked like the rest.
Wear the mask and demand proper protective gear.
Quit the job.

reference.rationale_short: Chemicals poison slowly and surely; gear is a right, not a majority vote.

state: A landlord demands the flat returned to original condition after 5 years of normal living.

options.text: Renovate the whole flat at your expense.
Return it clean; normal wear is not damage.
Leave it as is without cleaning.

reference.rationale_short: Normal wear is legally the landlord's cost; cleaning yes, renovation no.

state: A bus driver is shouted at by an aggressive fare-dodger.

options.text: Stop the bus and call the police.
Let the inspector handle it alone.
Throw the passenger out personally.

reference.rationale_short: The driver never leaves the cabin; a police call goes via dispatch while the inspector buys time talking.
